summary.text: Ryan Mackenzie is the Republican U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 7th District and lost re-election on November 3, 2026 to Bob Brooks; his term ends January 3, 2027.

First elected in 2024 when he defeated then-incumbent Susan Wild, he is a Lehigh Valley resident who previously worked in state government and served in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives from 2012 to 2024.
In Congress he serves on the Education and Workforce, Foreign Affairs and Homeland Security committees and chairs the Workforce Protections Subcommittee.

paragraphs.text: According to his official biography, Mackenzie is a ninth-generation resident of the Lehigh Valley, where his family has lived since colonial times.
He graduated from Parkland High School in 2000, earned a bachelor's degree in finance and international business from New York University in 2004 and an M.B.A. from Harvard in 2010.

Before elected office he worked at the U.S. Department of Labor in the Office of the Secretary, on political campaigns, and as policy director at the Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry, and he earned a real estate sales license.
Mackenzie won a special election on April 24, 2012 for Pennsylvania House District 134 and was re-elected in later cycles; after redistricting he represented District 187 from 2022 to 2024.
In the state House he was Republican chair of the Labor & Industry Committee and co-chair of the International Relations Caucus, and his official biography says he authored a dozen laws.
Mackenzie was elected to the U.S. House on November 5, 2024, defeating incumbent Democrat Susan Wild by 50% to 49%, according to Ballotpedia.

He has served on nonprofit and government boards, including local organizations for senior housing and autism services, Lehigh Career & Technical Institute, the Greater Lehigh Valley Chamber of Commerce, state workforce and economic development boards, and the President's Commission on White House Fellowships.
According to his official biography, he lives in the Lehigh Valley with his wife, Chloe, and their children.
During the campaign, his campaign website described him as running on tax relief, health care costs and housing affordability.
He received 43.9% of the vote to Bob Brooks's 56.1%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
